models_evaluated: ML-driven CDS peripheral arterial disease identification algorithm

links.outcome: Stakeholder-reported factors enabling real-world integration of ML-driven CDS
links.effect: Longitudinal, multidisciplinary stakeholder engagement and early consideration of end-user needs were identified as key to translating algorithm performance into real-world care.
links.quote: Longitudinal and multidisciplinary stakeholder engagement in the development and integration of ML-driven CDS underpins its effective translation into real-world care.

links.outcome: Stakeholder-reported barriers to ML-driven CDS integration, including feedback loops
links.effect: Lack of feedback loops, failure to incorporate on-the-ground context, and data silos were identified as negative factors of integration.
links.quote: Negative factors of integration included failure to incorporate the on-the-ground context, the lack of feedback loops, and data silos limiting the ML-driven CDS.

screen.reason: This is a qualitative empirical study exploring factors influencing the real-world clinical integration and workflow of a machine learning-driven clinical decision support tool for identifying peripheral arterial disease.
